    # Deterministic Clarke-Wright savings with orientation-aware merges
    # Initialize each customer as its own route
    routes = []
    belong = {}
    r_demand = []
    for rid, v in enumerate(cust_ids):

        belong[v] = rid
        r_demand.append(demands[v])

    def attempt_merge(i, j):
        nonlocal routes, belong, r_demand
        ra = belong.get(i, None)
        rb = belong.get(j, None)
        if ra is None or rb is None or ra == rb:
            return False
        A = routes[ra]
        B = routes[rb]
        # i and j must be at ends
        ia = 0
        while ia < len(A) and A[ia] != i:
            ia += 1
        ib = 0
        while ib < len(B) and B[ib] != j:
            ib += 1
        if ia < 0 or ib < 0:
            return False
        if not (ia == 0 or ia == len(A) - 1):
            return False
        if not (ib == 0 or ib == len(B) - 1):
            return False
        if r_demand[ra] + r_demand[rb] > cap:
            return False

        # Build merged route based on end orientations
        # Cases:
        # A: i at last/first; B: j at last/first
        a_first = (ia == 0)
        a_last = (ia == len(A) - 1)
        b_first = (ib == 0)
        b_last = (ib == len(B) - 1)

        if a_last and b_first:
            merged = A + B
        elif a_first and b_last:
            merged = B + A
        elif a_last and b_last:
            merged = A + B[::-1]
        else:  # a_first and b_first
            merged = A[::-1] + B

        # Update routes list in-place by removing one route deterministically
        # Remove route rb first to preserve ra index; but ra might be > rb
        # We'll mark routes as None and later compress.
        routes[ra] = merged
        r_demand[ra] = r_demand[ra] + r_demand[rb]
        # Update belong for customers in merged
        for v in merged:
            belong[v] = ra
        routes[rb] = None
        # r_demand[rb] left stale; will be ignored after compression
        return True

    for s, i, j in saving_items:

    new_routes = []
    new_r_demand = []
    route_index = {}
    for rid, r in enumerate(routes):
        if r is not None and len(r) > 0:
            route_index[rid] = len(new_routes)
            new_routes.append(r)
            new_r_demand.append(r_demand[rid])
    routes = new_routes
    r_demand = new_r_demand
    # Fix belong mapping
    for v in cust_ids:
        rid_old = belong[v]
        belong[v] = route_index.get(rid_old, None)

    # If some customers somehow unmapped (shouldn't), put them as singleton routes
    for v in cust_ids:
        if belong.get(v, None) is None:
            belong[v] = len(routes)
            routes.append([v])
            r_demand.append(demands[v])

    # Local improvements
    # Intra-route 2-opt (deterministic first-improvement)
    def two_opt(route):

        # Try all i<j, first improvement
        for i in range(m - 1):

                if delta < 0:

                    improved = True

        return improved
